newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end sharply up on JGB rally.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end sharply up on JGB rally.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen futures contract ended Wednesday's TIFFE day session sharply higher in sympathy with gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
The June contract closed at an intraday high of 99.30. The volume was 83,779 contracts.
Key December JGB futures surged to end at 126.04, up from 125.30 on Tuesday, but were off the intraday high of 126.30.

"The rise in Euroyen futures was fuelled by the rally in JGB futures. The June, however, failed to break the key 99.30 level, as the December JGB futures gave up some gains after rising one yen," said a trader at a city bank.
JGBs and Euroyen futures were boosted by the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment for November, which showed only a limited improvement in business sentiment.
A decline in the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) rate to an 11-month low of 0.50 percent also helped fuel the rally in the afternoon, traders said.
Three-month CDs were last issued at this level on December 22, 1995. The issuer was a major city bank and the volume was about 10 billion yen, traders said.
"The spread between the March and June Euroyen futures contracts is likely to shrink further and the yield curve should continue to flatten," said a trust bank trader.

As the volume of the September 1997 contract was a hefty 55,778 contracts today, the shift in the benchmark futures contract may come sooner than previously thought, the city bank trader said. The September ended up 0.08 at 99.14, after trading between 99.10 and 99.16.
The key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.48 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.
The BOJ injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
One-month and two-month CDs were offered at 0.49 percent and 0.50 percent respectively, both unchanged from the previous day.
Interest rate swap (IRS) rates were down sharply in line with the JGB rally, with the five-year IRS rate falling to 1.86/1.90 percent from 1.96/2.00 percent on Tuesday.
